domains_and_motifs.description: HMG box DNA-binding domain; recognizes DNA sequence 5'-xCTTTGATx-3' (Wnt Response Element); ~75 amino acid residues forming three alpha helices separated by loops

domains_and_motifs.name: C-clamp domain
domains_and_motifs.description: C-clamp DNA binding domain; bipartite motif with four characteristic cysteines and basic residue clusters; recognizes GC-rich Helper motif (5'-RCCGCC-3') adjacent to Wnt Response Elements; likely forms zinc finger structure; enables enhanced gene targeting and stronger transcriptional regulation

sources.notes: The TCF C-clamp DNA binding domain expands the Wnt transcriptome via alternative target recognition

function.uniprot_function: Participates in the Wnt signaling pathway and modulates MYC expression by binding to its promoter in a sequence-specific manner. Acts as repressor in the absence of CTNNB1, and as activator in its presence. Necessary for the terminal differentiation of epidermal cells, the formation of keratohyalin granules and the development of the barrier function of the epidermis. Involved in the positive regulation of chondrocyte differentiation. Key transcriptional effector of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway.
function.catalytic_activity: Not applicable - transcription factor, not an enzyme
function.tissue_specificity: Widely expressed with tissue-specific alternative splicing patterns. High expression in intestine (small intestine and colon epithelium, crypts to villi gradient), pancreas, pancreatic islets, liver, adipose tissue, skeletal muscle. Unique ex13-13b splicing form expressed in pancreatic islets, colon, and brain regions (hypothalamus/thalamus, occipital lobe). Expression pattern critical for glucose homeostasis and type 2 diabetes susceptibility.

pathways.pathway_role_summary: TCF7L2 is the major transcriptional effector of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. In the absence of Wnt ligands, TCF7L2 recruits corepressors (TLE/Groucho, CtBP) to actively repress target genes. Upon Wnt activation, beta-catenin accumulates in the nucleus, binds TCF7L2, displaces corepressors, and recruits coactivators (BCL9, CBP/p300) to activate transcription of Wnt target genes including MYC, CCND1, AXIN2. TCF7L2 also participates in crosstalk with TGF-beta signaling via interactions with SMAD3/4. Critical regulator of development, stem cell maintenance, glucose homeostasis, and cancer.

disease_associations.description: TCF7L2 variants (particularly rs7903146) are the strongest common genetic risk factor for type 2 diabetes in multiple populations; SNPs affect alternative splicing and expression levels; associated with impaired insulin secretion and glucose homeostasis
TCF7L2 is a key downstream effector of APC-beta-catenin mutations in colorectal cancer; drives expression of oncogenic Wnt target genes; nuclear localization correlates with tumor progression
TCF7L2 variants associated with prostate cancer risk; rs7903146 T allele shows inverse association with prostate cancer in some studies
TCF7L2 variants associated with familial breast cancer risk in some populations
De novo variants in TCF7L2 associated with developmental delay, intellectual disability, and brain malformations
TCF7L2 variants predict conversion to gestational diabetes in pregnancy

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive data available from multiple sources. Crystal structures available for beta-catenin binding domain and HMG box. Detailed kinetic data available for beta-catenin interaction. Extensive alternative splicing generates >30 isoforms with tissue-specific expression; canonical isoform (619 aa) used as reference. Some PTM sites may have alternative numbering in different isoforms. C-clamp domain coordinates are approximate; crystal structure not yet available. Kinetic parameters for most protein interactions not available in literature.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: TCF7L2 is essential for Wnt pathway modeling as the major transcriptional effector. Acts as molecular switch between repression (with TLE/CtBP) and activation (with beta-catenin/BCL9/CBP). Well-characterized kinetics for beta-catenin binding enable quantitative modeling. Multiple regulatory phosphorylation sites (NLK inhibitory, HIPK2 activating, TNIK activating) provide control points. Crosstalk with TGF-beta pathway via SMAD3 interactions. Disease relevance (diabetes, cancer) highlights importance for therapeutic modeling. Tissue-specific isoforms may require consideration for context-specific models.
